dataset_spec.name: uci_cdc_diabetes
dataset_spec.description: UCI CDC Diabetes Health Indicators (BRFSS 2015 telephone survey, binary balanced-free version; class-stratified subsample of 1000 for the readout, whole table for XGBoost). 21 self-reported health and lifestyle indicators. Binary diabetes (prediabetes or diabetes ever diagnosed).
dataset_spec.setting: Adult respondent to the 2015 US Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System telephone health survey. The observations are self-reported: ever told of high blood pressure or cholesterol, body mass index, smoking, cardiovascular history, physical activity, diet, alcohol use, healthcare access, general, mental and physical health, mobility, sex, age group, education and income.

highbp.text_label: Ever told by a health professional that blood pressure is high

highchol.text_label: Ever told that blood cholesterol is high

cholcheck.text_label: Cholesterol checked within the last 5 years

smoker.text_label: Smoked at least 100 cigarettes in lifetime

heartdiseaseorattack.text_label: Ever told of coronary heart disease or myocardial infarction

physactivity.text_label: Any physical activity in the past 30 days outside of work

fruits.text_label: Eats fruit one or more times per day

veggies.text_label: Eats vegetables one or more times per day

hvyalcoholconsump.text_label: Heavy drinker (more than 14 drinks per week for men, 7 for women)

anyhealthcare.text_label: Has any kind of health care coverage

nodocbccost.text_label: Could not see a doctor in the past 12 months because of cost

menthlth.text_label: Days of poor mental health in the past 30 days

physhlth.text_label: Days of poor physical health in the past 30 days

diffwalk.text_label: Serious difficulty walking or climbing stairs

text_values.1: Never attended school or only kindergarten
text_values.5: College 1 to 3 years (some college or technical school)

cdc_diabetes.question: Based on these survey answers, has this respondent ever been told by a health professional that they have diabetes or prediabetes?
